title: Count Special Subsequences
summary: Given an array of positive integers, count the number of distinct subsequences of length 4 where the product of the first and third elements equals the product of the second and fourth elements, and there is at least one element between each pair of indices.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, count the number of distinct subsequences of length 4 where the product of the first and third elements equals the product of the second and fourth elements, and there is at least one element between each pair of indices.
constraints: nums has 7–1,000 positive values up to 1,000.
Choose p<q<r<s with at least one unused index between each consecutive pair.
hints: The product equality is equivalent to the reduced ratio nums[p]/nums[q] equaling nums[s]/nums[r].
Sweep the second index while a frequency map holds eligible future third/fourth ratios.
Query all spaced first indices, then remove pairs whose third index will become too close for the next sweep step.
The map contains exactly the suffix pairs satisfying both future gaps, so each valid quadruple is counted at its unique second index.

tests.explanation: Indices 0,2,4,6 satisfy the gaps and products 1×3 = 3×1.
Only indices 0,2,4,6 meet all three spacing requirements, producing one valid subsequence.
